event_action: Departed Norfolk/Yorktown area for the Canal Zone and Pacific ports with Task Unit 29.2.5.
source_locator: DANFS, para. beginning 'Late in September'; War Cruise p.7

event_action: Passed through the Panama Canal; exact anchorage and lock timing not reconstructed.
Passed under the Golden Gate Bridge and anchored in San Francisco Bay.
Arrived Pearl Harbor, embarked mines and received routing for Funafuti.
Supported survey and mining of Funafuti approaches; supplied water, provisions, repairs, and medical services; laid mooring buoys.
Gunners fired on enemy aircraft for the first time during a Japanese raid on the Funafuti runway.
Loaded mines and gear for Tarawa.
Provided heavy equipment and mines to mine details at Tarawa amid recurring Japanese air activity.
Delivered mines and heavy equipment; New Year's Day 1944 was spent at Espiritu Santo.
Delivered advance-base mine equipment at Guadalcanal.
Surveyed lagoon passes and prepared a self-propelled barge to mine channels.
Brief Tarawa stop to embark Mine Detail 19 before returning to Pearl Harbor.
notes: Arrival date estimated from Makin departure on 28 Jan and departure for Pearl Harbor on 31 Jan.

event_action: Returned to Pearl Harbor and embarked passengers for San Francisco.
Three-day San Francisco stay after transporting more than 500 passengers.
Discharged passengers and prepared for Marshall Islands operations.
Majuro served as a recurring base for minelaying and logistics circuits to Kwajalein and Enewetak.
notes: This interval is represented by separate route legs and repeated point events.

event_action: First documented March circuit at Kwajalein.
Second documented Majuro–Kwajalein circuit.
Enewetak operations before return toward Hawaii.
notes: War Cruise gives 17–20 Apr for Enewetak–Pearl, but that duration is implausibly short and conflicts with DANFS departure on 22 Apr.

event_action: Pearl Harbor repairs, mine loading, and gunnery exercises.
notes: Arrival date estimated from normal transit after official 22 Apr departure from the Marshalls.

event_action: Returned to Majuro as part of ammunition, mine, and bomb supply circuits.
Makin logistics stop during the summer supply circuit.
Enewetak logistics; later carried American casualties and Japanese prisoners toward Pearl Harbor.
Pearl Harbor turnaround before another Enewetak/Marianas circuit.
Enewetak-based segment supporting the Marshalls and Marianas.
notes: War Cruise contains a likely erroneous pre-invasion 'Iwo Jima' entry for 1–4 Aug. The default map does not route Terror to Iwo Jima in 1944.

event_action: Guam-area cargo operations during the Marianas campaign.
notes: Exact inbound/outbound sequence is conflicted in the cruise-chart transcription.

event_action: Departed Oahu for the west coast; arrived San Francisco on 24 August.
San Francisco drydocking and overhaul.
Loaded mines and minesweeping gear before western Pacific deployment.
Saipan stop before Ulithi defensive mining operations.
Began defensive mining operations at Ulithi.
Repeated Saipan–Ulithi cargo and support circuits.
Cargo operations in the Admiralty Islands/Manus area.
notes: The chart transcription contains an improbable pre-invasion Iwo Jima leg; Manus is retained as the confirmed destination.

event_action: Pearl Harbor repairs and alterations to accommodate Commander, Mine Force, Pacific Fleet staff; assumed flagship duty 6 January 1945.
Arrived Enewetak, fueled, and continued toward Ulithi.
Supplied mines and gear to mine craft preparing for Iwo Jima.
Served as tender for mine craft at Tinian, the second staging area.
Directed and supported minesweeping; fired 5-inch guns at shore positions; received casualties and damaged small craft.
Transferred battle casualties to an Army hospital at Saipan.
Serviced and supplied mine craft staging for the assault on Okinawa.
Arrived off Kerama Retto on 24 March; anchored in the harbor on 29 March as flagship and tender.
Took two Japanese aircraft under fire during a harbor penetration; one aircraft splashed nearby.
Fought a four-hour mass air attack; helped down two aircraft and aided survivors of LST-447 and SS Logan Victory.
Fired on aircraft attacking nearby Pinckney, sent boats, and treated casualties.

coordinate_basis: Kerama Retto anchorage / published attack-area approximation
event_action: Kamikaze and bombs struck the ship shortly before 0400; 41 dead, 7 missing, and 123 wounded.
Moored to Natrona for emergency repairs; flag staff transferred before withdrawal.
Reached Saipan after withdrawal from Kerama Retto; forward-area repair judged inadequate.
Estimated Enewetak stop on the documented Saipan–Enewetak–Pearl Harbor withdrawal route.
notes: Intermediate dates are estimated; DANFS confirms the route but not the dates.

event_action: Arrived Pearl Harbor with visible kamikaze damage; departed for San Francisco after brief support.
notes: Capt. Blakeslee chart gives a later Pearl Harbor interval; NavSource photographic dating is used for mapping.

event_action: Reached San Francisco, unloaded ammunition, and prepared for shipyard overhaul.
Mare Island overhaul repaired kamikaze damage and strengthened antiaircraft armament.
Departed San Francisco Bay on the day Japan announced surrender, bound west via Hawaii and Saipan.
Reached Buckner Bay; Rear Admiral Arthur D. Struble established his headquarters aboard on 9 September.
notes: DANFS states the ship was moored in Buckner Bay on 16 Sep; the Album gives arrival on 8 Sep.

event_action: Rode out a severe typhoon; Patoka collided with Terror, causing moderate hull damage.
Survived a second severe typhoon and cared for hundreds of survivors from damaged, beached, or sunk mine-force vessels.
source_locator: Album p.6 and late-1945 chronology p.31

event_action: Served at Sasebo as Mine Force flagship/tender, supplying water, fuel, gear, and medical support to minesweepers.
Panamint came alongside for transfer of staff and equipment; Terror departed Sasebo for Pearl Harbor on 20 November.
Entered Pearl Harbor Navy Yard drydock and underwent repairs through February 1946.
source_locator: War Cruise late-1945 chronology p.31; Album p.6

event_action: Arrived in San Francisco Bay/Treasure Island after departing Pearl Harbor on 21 February.
notes: Exact February arrival date is not stated; 27 Feb is a modeling estimate.

event_action: Returned to Pearl Harbor; Commander Mine Force, Pacific Fleet flag shifted aboard before return to San Francisco.
notes: Compiled volume contains minor date discrepancies; detailed chronology gives 6–12 Mar outbound and 25 Mar departure.

event_action: Operated from Treasure Island as Mine Force Pacific flagship until the force was dissolved on 25 December 1946.
source_locator: War Cruise chronology p.41; Album p.6
